the_planner_cannot_plan_this: scripts/silver/plan_catalog_migration.py + CatalogMigrator.plan_table CANNOT emit this diff today, and that is by design, not a defect: migrate._glue_columns builds the DESIRED table from the contract's `glue_type` -- 'the CURRENT catalog type -- migrations here are additive/property, not the INV-2 widen' (its own docstring) -- so desired == live and plan_table returns NOOP. The sanctioned way to make the planner emit a widen is to move the contract's glue_type to the target FIRST (registry LEADS Glue, the f011_ddl_diff_report._MIGRATION_PENDING mechanism). That registry edit is deliberately NOT taken here: the owner applies the catalog first and the registry is REGENERATED from a re-captured R0 afterwards (the CONAB/tranche-2 apply-then-refresh precedent), so no hand-edited contract ever exists. scripts/ops/pinned_writer_widening_runbook.py builds the desired TableInput from the LIVE table instead, and hands the resulting plan to the SAME CatalogMigrator.apply_table.
partition_projection_note: PARTITION PROJECTION SURVIVES, and it survives because the TableInput carries it, not because update_table is gentle. update_table REPLACES the table definition: any Parameter omitted from the TableInput is GONE. MEASURED PROOF that this is a real hazard: the 2026-07-15 silver_noaa_oni apply used CatalogMigrator.build_desired_table, whose minimal TableInput dropped Owner ('hadoop' -> None), LastAccessTime, SkewedInfo and BucketColumns and moved NumberOfBuckets -1 -> 0 on that table -- read back live 2026-09-09. (It would NOT have dropped projection.*: plan_table overlays the live Parameters. But it drops other live fields.) The runbook therefore does not rebuild the TableInput from the contract at all: it takes the LIVE TableInput verbatim, drops only the read-only fields Glue rejects on input, and changes one Type token -- then ASSERTS json.dumps(Parameters, sort_keys=True) and json.dumps(PartitionKeys, sort_keys=True) are byte-identical before and after, and REFUSES the apply if they are not. The nine preserved Parameters are EXTERNAL, parquet.compression, projection.enabled, projection.leviathan_slug.type, projection.leviathan_slug.values, projection.marketing_year.range, projection.marketing_year.type, storage.location.template, transient_lastDdlTime.
partition_key_note: THE marketing_year PARTITION KEY STAYS `int` AND IS NOT PART OF THIS MIGRATION. It is a PROJECTED key (projection.marketing_year.type=integer, range 1982,2035): its values are parsed out of the S3 path by the storage.location.template, never read from the parquet body. The contract's int64 pin lives on physical_columns (the BODY column week_of_marketing_year); partition_keys[] carries glue_type int and is untouched. Nothing the pinned writer emits can change a projected key's type, and CatalogMigrator._unsafe_diffs refuses any partition-key change outright -- so a plan that touched it would be refused, not applied.

The workgroup that runs every query is `primary` -- the only workgroup in the account (MEASURED 2026-09-09 athena.list_work_groups) -- and athena.get_work_group(WorkGroup='primary')['WorkGroup']['Configuration']['EngineVersion'] reads {'EffectiveEngineVersion': 'Athena engine version 3', 'SelectedEngineVersion': 'AUTO'}, so the reader is engine v3 and its documented Parquet behaviour is to coerce a narrower stored integer up to the declared wider column. arm_vs_flip_note: There is nothing to arm. No new column, no new partition, no new slug, no producer change -- the producer bytes are already pinned by commit 3f5f4720 and are unchanged by this file. This migration moves ONE catalog type token so that the pin the writer already carries becomes legal. It is the DEBT the pin created, being paid.
known_limitation: This widen makes the catalog able to receive the pinned writer's output; it does not make the promote happen, and it does not rewrite a byte. Until the canonical rewrite runs, silver_fgis is a bigint catalog over INT32 objects -- the state the coercion_note covers. Also note that the two silver jobdefs must not be repinned past fbe6a7cb until BOTH this and the silver_modis_ndvi widen have landed; this file closes one half of that hold, not the hold.
rollback_note: ONE update_table back, through the RESTORE path. The narrow definition is week_of_marketing_year `int` with every other field unchanged: `python scripts/ops/pinned_writer_widening_runbook.py --table silver_fgis --rollback` re-reads live, refuses unless the column is exactly `bigint`, asserts Parameters/PartitionKeys byte-identity again, and applies the reverse plan through CatalogMigrator.restore_table. The equivalent DDL is `ALTER TABLE leviathan_dev.silver_fgis REPLACE COLUMNS (week_of_marketing_year int, week_ending_date date, destination_country string, exports_mt_weekly double, exports_mt_ctd double, source string);`. THE ROLLBACK IS NOT apply_table, AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT STYLISTIC. A reverse plan is a NARROWING; leviathan.silver.types.is_narrowing_change returns True for ALL ELEVEN reverse directions across both tables (bigint->int, bigint->smallint, bigint->tinyint, double->float, MEASURED 2026-09-10), and CatalogMigrator.apply_table raises UnsafeMigration on any narrowing. A rollback routed through apply_table would therefore be a DEAD COMMAND -- it refuses, and nothing is restored. --rollback instead goes through CatalogMigrator.restore_table, the sanctioned reverse path (leviathan.silver.types names the precedent in its own comment: B2's F036 int->bigint 'had to detour through restore_table for the same false NARROW'). The narrowing override this represents is BOUNDED: the run refuses unless the unsafe set is EXACTLY the expected NARROW entries for exactly the debt columns -- a DROP, a partition-key change or any other column narrowing still stops it. The restore basis is the LIVE table with only those Type tokens reversed (not the R0 sidecar), so unrelated catalog drift is never reverted; restore_table refuses if the live hash moved since the plan was cut and verifies the post-restore hash itself. MEASURED END TO END 2026-09-10, AWS-FREE: narrow -> --apply -> wide -> --rollback -> narrow against the estate's own in-memory Glue/S3 fakes with a REAL leviathan.silver.lease.Lease, driving the runbook's real apply() -- both directions returned 0, all eleven columns came back to their narrow types, Parameters and PartitionKeys were byte-identical to the pre-apply state (all five projection.* keys plus storage.location.template present), and exactly four update_table calls were issued. The deck test tests/unit/silver/test_pinned_writer_widening_migration.py::test_the_rollback_actually_restores_a_wide_catalog is that round trip. restore_table writes no machine manifest of its own, so the runbook writes a <UTC>_<table>_rollback_restore.json record beside these files carrying the pre-rollback (wide) TableInput as the backup. No parquet object is touched by the apply or by the rollback, in either direction.
